findings.description: The unchanged-tree check compares status entries rather than file contents. Overwriting an already modified tracked file leaves the same porcelain entry, so the helper reports success despite changing the main tree.
findings.failure_mode: If a main-tree file already has status ' M', a probe can overwrite that file through its absolute path. Both status snapshots remain identical and the helper exits 0, silently accepting destruction of existing edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare content fingerprints before and after the probe, including files already dirty at entry, or enforce filesystem isolation that prevents writes to the main tree.

findings.description: The probe runs arbitrary commands in a linked worktree whose Git metadata and refs are shared with the main repository. The status comparison does not detect mutations to other branch refs, repository configuration, or hooks.
findings.failure_mode: A probe running 'git update-ref refs/heads/other-branch HEAD' can overwrite an existing branch pointer while leaving the main tree's status unchanged. The helper exits 0 and its cleanup does not restore the ref.
findings.suggested_fix: Run probes in an independent disposable repository with separate Git metadata, and restrict access to the original repository.

findings.description: The --consumed-by path accepts a map in any status, although the command's unattended exception is restricted to handed-off maps. It performs no status or unresolved-row validation before closing.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended invocation against a charting map enters the rejection loop for every open decision row, closes its tickets and epic, and marks the map closed without completing the operator's decisions.
findings.suggested_fix: Before any mutation, require a handed-off map with no unresolved rows for --consumed-by. Allow a completed close to be retried idempotently for the same cycle.

findings.description: op_close with --consumed-by has no precondition at all: it does not check that the map doc Status is `handed-off`, does not check that the frontier is empty, and skips the dec-write-lib context check that the --reason branch performs. chart-guard.sh --close-consumed likewise passes in an unattended context for any map. chart.md (head) documents the exception as applying only 'on a handed-off map', and plan-and-analyze.md tells an unattended run to call `/chart close <slug> --consumed-by <cycle-id>` after the PRD is written. The close loop then rejects every `open` ledger row (`dw reject ... map closed`), closes every bead and the epic, and sets Status `closed`.
findings.failure_mode: An autonomous /plan-and-analyze (or any agent) that picks the wrong slug, or runs while a map is still `charting`, irreversibly rejects every undecided decision row on that map, closes all its question beads and the epic, and marks the map consumed. The in-progress chart is destroyed with no operator in the loop, which is exactly what PRD D12 / SDD D-4.3 say may not happen.
findings.suggested_fix: In op_close, when --consumed-by is given: require `doc_field Status` == `handed-off` (die otherwise with 'only a handed-off map is consumed'), and die if `map_rows` still contains open rows. Keep the interactive-context requirement for every other close. Optionally make chart-guard.sh --close-consumed take --map and perform the same Status check so the guard is also correct.

findings.description: section_append passes operator/agent text to awk via `-v line="$2"`. POSIX awk (gawk, mawk, BWK) processes escape sequences in -v assignments, so a literal backslash sequence in --line, --name, --why, or a bead title becomes a real newline, tab, etc. san1() strips C0/C1 control characters and flattens whitespace but leaves backslashes untouched, so `\n` survives sanitisation and is expanded inside awk. Callers: op_resolve (`- ${name} (${row}, ${BEAD}): ${line}`), op_rule_out (`- ${title}: ${why}`).
findings.failure_mode:
A decision line that legitimately contains a backslash (a Windows path like `C:
ew	asks`, a regex such as `\d+`, or text quoting an escape) corrupts the tracked map doc: `
` inserts a new line and `	` a tab, breaking the one-bullet-per-decision shape. Text sourced from a research report that contains `
## Decisions so far
- Forged (DEC-9999, x): ...` forges additional 'settled' decisions that op_handoff inlines into the priority-1 context snapshot that /plan-and-analyze reads as 'confirm, do not re-ask'.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not pass free text through `awk -v`. Either escape backslashes first (`line="${2//\\/\\\\}"`) or pass the value via the environment and read it with `ENVIRON["LINE"]` inside the awk program (`LINE="$2" awk '...'`). Also have san1() reject or escape backslashes so the tracked doc stays one plain line per bullet.

findings.cross_file_justification: The scope check in chart-ticket.sh (research-begin/-end) and the main-tree check in chart-unblock-probe.sh both rely on `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching`. Per git-status(1), in `matching` mode a directory that matches an ignore pattern is shown as one entry and paths inside it are NOT shown. op_handoff writes its snapshot to grimoires/loa/context/ and chart.md marks maps and research as '(tracked)' but not the snapshot, consistent with the repo .gitignore pattern `grimoires/loa/context/` noted by the primary reviewer. plan-and-analyze.md (diff) auto-loads `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` as priority-1 'settled decisions'.
findings.description: Both before/after snapshots show `!! grimoires/loa/context/` as a single line regardless of what is created or modified inside it. A research subagent (diff version has the Write tool) or an unblock probe that writes `grimoires/loa/context/chart-<anything>.md`, or edits an existing snapshot, produces identical before/after output, so research-end and the probe exit 0. The same blind spot applies to any other dir-pattern-ignored path. The checks in both scripts are documented as the mechanism that makes 'the ticket fails' when writes escape grimoires/loa/research/.
findings.failure_mode: Prompt-injected research content (WebFetch) or a probe command plants or rewrites a hand-off snapshot. The guard passes, and the next /plan-and-analyze ingests the planted file as priority-1 settled context with instructions to 'confirm, do not re-ask'. The declared containment property of research tickets and unblock probes is false for the one directory that drives downstream planning.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the status-only snapshot with a content fingerprint of the directories that matter: e.g. `find grimoires/loa/context grimoires/loa/maps .claude -type f -printf '%p %s %T@\n' | sort` (or `sha256sum` of the files) taken before and after, in addition to git status. Alternatively run `git status --ignored` (traditional mode) which lists individual ignored files. In head, keeping the researcher without a Write tool is the right call, but the probe path still needs the stronger check.

findings.description: The probe runs arbitrary argv in a `git worktree add --detach` checkout. A linked worktree shares the main repository's .git (refs, config, hooks, objects, remotes) and inherits the full session environment. The only verdict is a comparison of the main tree's `git status --porcelain`, which does not reflect ref rewrites (`git branch -f main <sha>`, `git update-ref`), `git push`, config edits, hook installs under .git/hooks, stash/reflog changes, or edits to tracked files that were already listed as modified before the probe (a dirty tree masks a changed ` M path` line). The header promises 'exits 1 when the main tree's status changed', which is literally true, but the SDD D-4.12 property it stands for ('never writes App-Zone code in the main tree') is not what is being checked.
findings.failure_mode: A probe command can rewrite or push branches, install hooks that run on the operator's next commit, or overwrite an already-dirty tracked file, and the helper reports `exit 0` so the ticket passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the probe in a tree that has no link to the main .git: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$SCRATCH/wt"` (or `git clone --shared --no-hardlinks` into scratch and unset GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE). If a worktree is kept, also snapshot and compare `git for-each-ref`, `git config --list --local`, a hash of .git/hooks, and `git diff HEAD --stat` of tracked files before/after, and run the probe with a scrubbed environment (`env -i PATH=... HOME=$SCRATCH`).

findings.cross_file_justification: chart-frontier.sh (FILTER) and chart-ticket.sh bead_row both read the type as `.issue_type // .type`, i.e. the same PR treats a br payload that uses `type` instead of `issue_type` as possible. get-ready-work.sh filters on `.issue_type` only.
findings.description: The build-path exclusion that implement.md and implementing-tasks/SKILL.md now rely on ('drops question beads, which bare br ready would list') keys on `.issue_type` alone. If the installed br emits `type` (the shape the other two new scripts hedge for), `(.issue_type // "") != "question"` is true for every bead and no filtering happens.
findings.failure_mode: Decision tickets from /chart appear in /implement and /run work selection, defeating 'its tickets cannot enter a sprint' silently (no error, no warning).
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same expression as chart-frontier.sh: `map(select(((.issue_type // .type // "") | ascii_downcase) != "question"))`, and add a bats case with a `type`-shaped fixture.

findings.description: The map-epic detector unwraps only a top-level array. chart-ticket.sh first_obj also unwraps an `{"issues":[...]}` envelope, so that shape is expected from some br versions. For the envelope, `.labels` is null, the jq yields "no", and the script proceeds to create a sprint task under a map epic. Likewise a reply with no `labels` key at all is treated as 'not a map' rather than 'unknown', although the comment says an unreadable reply must refuse.
findings.failure_mode: A build task is created under a /chart map epic (the exact case the new guard exists to prevent), with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the first_obj logic (`elif type == "object" and has("issues") then .issues[0]`), and emit "unknown" when the unwrapped object lacks `labels` or `id`, so the existing refuse-on-unknown branch fires.

findings.description: The interactive-only rule is enforced in the script layer only for `close --reason`. epic, ticket, resolve, rule-out, handoff, research-begin/-end write ledger rows, beads and the tracked map doc with no context check; the rule depends on the skill prose calling chart-guard.sh first. dec-write-lib `new`/`decide` work unattended (it drops --answer-ref), so an autonomous session that skips step 0 can create a map, invent tickets, 'resolve' them to proposed rows, and hand the map off as settled priority-1 context.
findings.failure_mode: An unattended run produces a map 'whose rounds the agent answered', which SDD D-4.3 says is not a map, and the hand-off snapshot is consumed by the next PRD as settled.
findings.suggested_fix: Call the same `"$DW" context` check at the top of every mutating subcommand (all except research-end's read-only path and close --consumed-by, which needs its own Status precondition per DISS-001); refuse when the context is not `interactive`.

findings.description: context_files declares `grimoires/loa/context/chart-*.md` at priority 1 and the pre-existing `grimoires/loa/context/*.md` glob at priority 2, so every hand-off snapshot is auto-loaded twice and before Phase 0 runs. The Phase 0 prose says only the resolved snapshot is read and 'other snapshots are not ingested', and that with several snapshots unattended the run must stop and write nothing. The declarative loader contradicts both. Snapshots also inline research reports (sanitised) and unfenced ledger free text, which then arrive labelled 'settled decisions; confirm, do not re-ask'.
findings.failure_mode: With two open maps, the PRD is seeded with the decisions of both, including a map the operator did not choose, and the unattended stop rule cannot fire because ingestion already happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the priority-1 chart-*.md glob (and exclude chart-*.md from the priority-2 glob) and load the single resolved snapshot explicitly in Phase 0 after golden_resolve_open_map returns.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff's chart-researcher.md grants `tools: [Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, Write]` and agent-types.yaml marks it `write_capable: true`; the head full-file copy of chart-researcher.md has no Write tool and says the session saves the report. The two artifacts disagree.
findings.description: Either the agent keeps Write, in which case a WebFetch-exposed subagent has an unrestricted Write tool constrained only by prose ('exactly one file'), with the scope check blind to ignored directories (DISS-003); or the agent has no Write, in which case `write_capable: true` is wrong and any policy keyed on agent-types.yaml treats it as a writer.
findings.failure_mode: Stale capability metadata or an over-privileged research agent, depending on which file is authoritative.
findings.suggested_fix: Settle on the read-only agent (head version) and set `write_capable: false`; add the report-save step to the charting-decisions SKILL and research-end so the session, not the subagent, writes grimoires/loa/research/chart-<slug>-<ticket>.md.

findings.description: SP-1 explicitly exempts the create forms: `git checkout -b feature spike/x` and `git checkout -B feature spike/x` pass (`create=1 → continue`), yet each puts the spike's full tree on a new non-spike branch, which is the thing D-5.4 forbids. `git reset --hard spike/x` (copies the spike tree into the current branch's working tree and index) is also unmatched: it is neither in the merge|rebase|pull|cherry-pick group nor a checkout/restore. The header lists several misses but not these two, so they are not 'accepted edges'.
findings.failure_mode: Spike content enters a feature branch through an allowed command and later reaches a PR; the fence that ICE and this hook claim to provide does not fire.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat `-b`/`-B`/`--orphan` with a spike start-point as blocked (only `git checkout spike/x` and `git checkout -b spike/x` style creates on the spike itself should pass), and add `reset` (with --hard|--mixed|--soft or a bare ref) to the blocked verb group when a spike ref is named.

findings.description: Idempotency for `epic` is keyed only on the map doc existing. `br create` runs first; if writing the doc then fails (mkdir/mktemp/mv error, disk full, permission), the epic bead exists but no doc does, and a re-run calls `br create` again. The header promises 'a re-run ... creates only what is missing', which holds for ticket (lookup by external_ref) but not for epic.
findings.failure_mode: Duplicate `map` epics for one slug; chart-frontier and later `/chart <slug>` bind to whichever one the doc eventually names, orphaning the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Before `br create`, look up an existing epic via `br list --type epic --json` filtered on label `map` and slug `map-<slug>` (or description containing the map path) and reuse its id; only create when none is found.

findings.description: The hand-off snapshot inlines the map doc and `dw list --format md` output unfenced; only research reports go through the L6 sanitiser. Ledger summaries/rationales and map-doc free text are agent-composed from operator and research input and carry no 'untrusted' marker in the snapshot, although the snapshot header tells the consumer to treat its content as settled. The heading-demotion `sed -E 's/^(#+) /#\1 /'` also rewrites `#` lines inside fenced code blocks in the map doc.
findings.failure_mode: Instruction-like text that reached a ledger row or map bullet (via DISS-002 or ordinary copy from a report) is presented to /plan-and-analyze as authoritative priority-1 context without the fence applied to research.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the inlined map doc and ledger markdown through the same sanitize_for_session_start path (or wrap them in the UNTRUSTED fence used for reports), and perform heading demotion with an awk that tracks ``` fences.

findings.description: The FR-1.1 exemption for `git branch -D spike/<slug>` is decided by reading grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml from the working tree, not from HEAD or origin. The agent can edit that file directly with the Write/Edit tool (the ledger-writer discipline is prose), add a row with `status: decided`, `source: grimoires/loa/spikes/<slug>.md`, and a `to: decided, by: operator:x` transition, and the hook then allows the force-delete. The hook also does not check that the spike branch is present on a remote, although the comment's rationale ('pushed, never merged') assumes it is.
findings.failure_mode: An unpushed spike branch with unmerged commits is force-deleted after a forged or premature working-tree ledger edit; the prototype that the decision points to is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Read the ledger from the committed tree (`git show HEAD:grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`) and additionally require `git rev-parse -q --verify refs/remotes/origin/spike/<slug>` to succeed (the branch is on the remote) before exempting the delete.
